standard.title: Colons and brackets
standard.description: Understand the use of punctuation including colons and brackets to support meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how commas are used in lists, to separate clauses and in dialogue (AC9E6LA09). They have not yet worked with colons or brackets — punctuation marks that introduce, expand or parenthesise information rather than separating clauses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how colons and brackets support meaning.

nodes.label: Colon uses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the uses of colons and explain what each use signals to the reader
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a colon in a given sentence and explain what it signals — introduction of a list, elaboration of a preceding clause, or introduction of a quotation or example
nodes.typical_width: Examine colons in several sentences across different uses and explain how each signals a specific relationship between what comes before and after the colon
wider: Examine the impact of information added to sentences when colons are used — compare a sentence with and without the colon-introduced elaboration and discuss how meaning changes
Experiment with writing sentences where a colon introduces a list, an elaboration, and a quotation — discuss how the reader's expectation changes depending on what follows the colon

response_modes.reason: Colon usage is a precision skill with a small set of rules that students apply inconsistently — particularly confusing colon-before-list with comma-before-list. Practice across the distinct uses builds reliable application.

success_criteria: Identifies a colon in a given sentence
Explains what the colon signals in that specific context

nodes.label: Bracket uses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how brackets are used to add parenthetical information and explain what effect this has on meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Identify brackets in a given sentence and explain what the bracketed information adds — clarification, aside, example, or attribution; explain why the information is parenthetical rather than integrated into the main clause
nodes.typical_width: Compare sentences that use brackets with versions where the parenthetical content is removed or integrated into the main clause; discuss how the choice to bracket information affects the reader's experience of it
wider: Examine how the impact of bracketed information differs from information added through commas or dashes — when does a writer choose brackets over other parenthetical punctuation?
Investigate how brackets are used in academic and informational writing vs creative writing — do the purposes differ?

response_modes.reason: Students commonly add brackets without understanding why information is parenthetical — they treat brackets as interchangeable with commas. The reasoning scaffold — why is this information outside the main clause rather than inside it, and what effect does that have on how the reader processes it — is what makes bracket use purposeful rather than mechanical.

success_criteria: Identifies bracketed information in a given sentence
Explains why the information is parenthetical and what it adds to meaning
